title: From a list of integers, keep only numbers greater than a threshold and convert each to its `String` form (`filter(...).map(String::valueOf)`).
shortTitle: From a list of integers, keep only numbers greater than a threshold and convert each to its String form
keyPoints: filter(n -> n > threshold).map(String::valueOf) keeps values above the cutoff and converts to string
Filter before map so the conversion only runs on retained elements
String.valueOf safely converts Integer including null (produces the text 'null')
Decide whether the threshold is strict (>) or inclusive (>=) based on the business rule
This filter-then-map shape is one of the most common stream pipelines
Filter nulls explicitly before the comparison to avoid NullPointerException on unboxing

s1_definition.oneliner: filter(n -> n > threshold) keeps values above the cutoff, then map(String::valueOf) converts each survivor to its decimal string representation.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **filter(n -> n > threshold)** keeps elements strictly above the threshold.
- **map(String::valueOf)** converts each surviving Integer to its decimal string.
- **Filter before map** avoids wasted conversions on discarded elements.
- **Null safety**: filter nulls first; unboxing null Integer to int throws NullPointerException.
- **Threshold semantics**: decide strict (>) or inclusive (>=) based on the business rule.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya at the National Bank of India keeps only transaction amounts above a reporting cutoff and renders them as text for a display panel that shows high-value transactions.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  List: [25000, 50000, 75000, 100000, 150000, 200000]
       │
       │  .filter(n -> n > 50000)
       ▼
  [75000, 100000, 150000, 200000]  (4 elements pass)
       │
       │  .map(String::valueOf)  (converts only 4 elements)
       ▼
  ["75000", "100000", "150000", "200000"]

  Key: filter BEFORE map = fewer conversions
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Filtering numbers above a threshold and converting to strings uses the filter-then-map pattern: filter first to shrink the stream, then map only the survivors to strings. This avoids wasted conversions on values that will be discarded.

Decide whether the threshold is strict (>) or inclusive (>=) based on the business rule, and filter nulls explicitly before the comparison to avoid NullPointerException from unboxing. At the National Bank of India, Priya used this for a display panel showing only high-value transaction amounts rendered as text.

This filter-then-map shape is one of the most common pipelines, and placing the cheap, selective filter first is a simple but real optimization.

Remember one sentence: filter before map so the expensive conversion runs only on retained elements, and always filter nulls before unboxing comparisons.
